skill.summary: Run a two-track code review against standards and product requirements.

remediation.suggestion: Require the agent to validate the fixed point with git rev-parse and pass git arguments without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: External git commands are part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Document that generated commands must quote or structure user-provided refs and reject shell metacharacters.

content.user_title: Review code changes against standards and specs
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss either project standards or product requirements. This skill compares a git diff against both sources and reports the results separately.
actual_capabilities: Reviews changes between HEAD and a user-supplied fixed point.
Checks changed code against repository coding standards.
Applies a Fowler code-smell baseline when repository standards are missing.
Looks for the originating issue, PRD, or spec source.
Runs standards and spec checks in separate subagents.
Reports the two review tracks under separate headings.
limitations: Requires a valid git fixed point before review can start.
Spec review is limited when no issue, PRD, or spec is available.
Depends on repository documentation for project-specific standards.
Does not run tests or prove runtime behavior by itself.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request branch
use_cases.description: Compare a feature branch with main and separate standards issues from requirement gaps.

use_cases.title: Check implementation against a PRD
use_cases.description: Verify that changed code follows the product request without mixing in style findings.

use_cases.title: Audit work before handoff
use_cases.description: Summarize review findings before another developer or AI agent continues the work.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent branch work
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with a common base branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch since main. Report standards findings and spec findings separately.

prompt_templates.title: Review against an issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Review changes that reference a tracked issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since origin/main and use the linked issue as the spec source. Separate hard violations from judgement calls.

prompt_templates.title: Review with a spec path
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a known local requirements document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since HEAD~5 using docs/feature-spec.md as the spec. Include any scope creep or missing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review with custom standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with explicit standards sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since release-candidate. Use CONTRIBUTING.md and CODING_STANDARDS.md as standards sources, then compare the diff with the PRD.

output_examples.input: Review since main for a feature branch with a linked issue.
output: Standards: one judgement-call smell about duplicated validation logic.
Spec: one missing requirement from the linked issue.
Summary: Standards has one finding. Spec has one finding.

output_examples.input: Review since HEAD~3 with no available spec.
output: Standards: reports documented standard violations and baseline smells.
Spec: skipped because no spec source was available.
Summary: Standards findings are counted separately from the skipped spec track.

best_practices: Provide the exact fixed point before starting the review.
Point the skill to the issue, PRD, or spec when it is not obvious.
Keep standards documents current so review findings match the repository.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for tests or runtime verification.
Do not merge standards and spec findings into one ranked list.
Do not ask for broad repository review when only a focused diff is needed.

faq.question: What fixed point should I provide?
faq.answer: Use the branch, commit, tag, or merge-base that represents the start of the changes you want reviewed.

faq.question: Does the skill need a spec?
faq.answer: A spec improves the Spec review. If none exists, the skill can skip that axis and report why.

faq.question: How are standards findings chosen?
faq.answer: The skill uses repository standards first, then applies a fixed code-smell baseline as judgement-call guidance.

faq.question: Does it run code or tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill reviews the diff and related documents. Test execution requires a separate request.

faq.question: Why are there two review sections?
faq.answer: Standards and Spec answer different questions. Keeping them separate prevents one type of issue from hiding the other.

faq.question: Can it review work in progress?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review any non-empty diff from HEAD back to a valid fixed point.
